changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/8067-component-input-member-kind.md`

- names `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` → `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` — edited by this change

  > A registration's `type: 'array'` said a value was a list and stopped there, so a member that drifted from `@objectstack/spec` was invisible to every layer that reads a declaration. `page:header.actions` is the measured cost: the contract declares `z.array(z.string())` ("Action IDs"), the renderer read the members as `ActionDef` objects, and the repo-wide parity gate in `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` stayed green for the whole life of the drift because both sides carried the key and neither could say what was inside it. What settled it was a maintainer ruling, not a test — and even after the fix, "these are ids" survived only as English in the registration's `description`.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `cf38a6cec` (merge-base with origin/main): 11 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1956 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2578 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36951613126)

Isolated at-tier reviewer, 2026-10-02T01:30Z. Inputs: card #11168 (body and all 31 comments), PR #11422 (body, 15-file list, net diff against `main` at the head), the head's check-runs, the head's files read with `git show`, and the 17.5.0 row read from objectstack `0f6dcac5e9` (`packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts`, `ObjectTimelinePropsSchema`).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The guard.** `@object-ui/plugin-timeline` is eager-imported; `object-timeline` joins `MINOR_17_5_LOADED_BLOCKS`; its OWED row leaves `UNJUDGED_SPEC_BLOCKS`, which keeps nine entries, all RETIRED / EMPTY / NOT REGISTERED; `registeredButUnloaded` expects `[]` again. Caps `0 / 0 / 3 / 0 / 0` equal the live ledgers; census `39 + 7 + 9 = 55`; owner `objectui#11168` 3 (`action:button` `endpoint` + `undoable`, `action:icon` `endpoint`). RIGHT, read against the head's `OBJECTUI_11111_LEDGER_CAPS`, the ledger and the three census pins.

2. **The ten inputs, on both tags through `OBJECT_TIMELINE_INPUTS`**, each read against `ObjectTimeline.tsx` / `renderer.tsx` at the head and the installed row's describe:
   - `timeline` (object): `timelineConfig?.member ?? mapping ?? flat` (`ObjectTimeline.tsx:551-581`); `scale` reaches the gantt branch only (`:809`, `:934`). Describe prefix verbatim; every sentence after it is a measured read. RIGHT.
   - `limit` (number): `resolveRowLimit` + `describeRefusedRowLimit` (`:69-96`, `:483`). Verbatim prefix. RIGHT.
   - `data` (array): `rawData = props.data || boundData || fetchedData` (`:544`), `fetchesForItself` gates on `!props.data` (`:415`). Verbatim prefix. RIGHT. Declaring it `array` reports a non-array as `type-mismatch`, which the row refuses too. RIGHT.
   - `items` (array): `effectiveItems` returns `schema.items` first (`:587`); `TimelineFeedItem` / `TimelineGanttItem` exist in `@object-ui/types` `data-display.ts`. Verbatim prefix. RIGHT.
   - `dateFormat` (enum `short` / `long` / `iso`): `renderer.tsx` `formatDate`, default `'short'` (`:1569`). Verbatim. RIGHT. An off-list value is now an `invalid-enum` error; the row refuses it. RIGHT.
   - `rowLabel` (string): `schema.rowLabel || t('timeline.gantt.rowLabel')` in the gantt branch only (`renderer.tsx:1869`). Verbatim prefix. RIGHT.
   - `minDate` / `maxDate` (string): `schema.minDate || dateRange.minDate` (`:1808-1809`); `findUnusableGanttDate` judges only a truthy pin; the inverted range is refused by name (`:1855`). Verbatim prefix. RIGHT.
   - `descriptionField` (string): `descField = mapping?.description ?? descriptionField ?? 'description'` (`:578`). The describe's first sentence is kept; its second ("the only spelling this binding has") is false of the renderer and of the same row's `mapping` describe. A description may say less than its describe, never more, so this is the right cut. RIGHT.
   - `mapping` (object; the row says `z.unknown()`, so `object` is inside its accept set): `title` / `date` between the block and the flat keys (`:551`, `:574-576`), `description` first (`:578`), `variant` the only spelling (`:579`); on the vertical rail `item.color` overrides the variant class (`renderer.tsx:1610`). Verbatim prefix. RIGHT.
   - `objectName` loses `required`: the row has it optional, and the renderer draws from `items`, `data` and `bind` with no object (`:415`, `:544`, `:587`). RIGHT for drawing; its reach into `navigation` is item 4.
   - `sort` rewrite: composed entries are sorted by start date (`:729-733`), so the key orders `$orderby` only; "Entry order" was false. RIGHT.
   - `view:timeline` publishes the same list: one renderer, and the guard judges `object-timeline` only, the `filter` / `sort` / `navigation` precedent in the same file. RIGHT.

3. **Kanban / calendar `navigation`:** "`openNewTab: true` … outranks every mode except `none`". `useNavigationOverlay.ts` returns on `mode === 'none' || navigation.preventNavigation` before the `mode === 'new_window' || navigation.openNewTab` branch; each pin holds both halves (four overlay rows plus the `none` row). RIGHT.

4. **WRONG, the finding.** `TIMELINE_NAVIGATION_DESCRIPTION`, which this diff re-emits as a member of `OBJECT_TIMELINE_INPUTS` on both tags, states that `page` and a mode-less block "open the record page through the record navigator the host publishes", and that `new_window` / `openNewTab` "open the record page in a new tab", with a host that publishes none as the only stated exception. This diff makes a timeline that names no `objectName` an accepted document on both tags (the pin's `diagnose({ type, items })` and `diagnose({ type, timeline, data })` rows read `[]` where the base raised `missing-required-prop`), and the new `objectName` description invites it ("issues no query and needs none"). On such a timeline the hook's `page` branch is `if (objectName && openRecord)`, so nothing opens, navigator mounted or not; and its `new_window` / `openNewTab` branch builds `/${encodedId}` with no object segment, which is not the record page. The sibling description this card already corrected carries the clause (`plugin-map/src/index.tsx:122`: "or on a map that names no `objectName`, there is no record page to open and the click opens nothing", from record `5928833509`'s round); the timeline's does not, and nothing pins the object-less case (`timelineNavigationMembers-8654` mounts `objectName: OBJECT` on every row, and so does the new pin's navigation row). At the base the clause was true of every validator-clean timeline; this diff is what makes it claim more than the renderer does. Fix, one round: the map's clause in `TIMELINE_NAVIGATION_DESCRIPTION`; one qualifying clause in `TIMELINE_OBJECT_NAME_DESCRIPTION` (it needs none to draw; `navigation`'s `page` / `new_window` still read it); one pin row per arm (a `data`-only block with `{ mode: 'page' }` under the navigator host opens nothing; `{ mode: 'new_window' }` opens no record page); the README / docs-page `page` sentence and the `object-timeline.navigation` `MEMBER_PINS` text follow.

5. **`ObjectTimelineProps.navigation` JSDoc** (published: `exports["."].types` is `dist/index.d.ts`, which re-exports the type): the hook's no-config branch calls only `onNavigate`; `ObjectTimeline` passes `onRowClick: onRowClick ?? onItemClick` and no `onNavigate` (`:802-806`); `openRecord` is read in the `page` branch alone, which an absent key never reaches; a mode-less block takes `navigation?.mode ?? 'page'` and `openRecord(objectName, id)`. The JSDoc states exactly this, and the new pin's last describe holds the pair. RIGHT.

6. **Eight `MEMBER_PINS` rows**, each file read end to end at the head. `timeline` / `data` / `items` / `mapping` / `filter` / `sort` → `objectTimelineInputs-11168.test.tsx`: every sentence of each `pins` claim has a row behind it. `navigation` → `timelineNavigationMembers-8654.test.tsx` (booking (c)): drawer lit control, modal / popover, `split` nothing, absent nothing with and without a navigator, `none` / `preventNavigation`, `new_window` / `openNewTab` with the four overlay rows and the `none` row, size / width, parent handler, `page` / mode-less under the navigator. `dataSource` → `ObjectTimeline.elementDataSource.test.tsx`: object from the binding, view filter / sort / pageSize to `$filter` / `$orderby` / `$top`, binding filter ANDed with sort / limit overriding, block filter ANDed with both, unresolvable view reports, no binding queries `objectName` with `$top` 100. It is in the population because `withElementDataSourceInput` injects `ELEMENT_DATA_SOURCE_INPUT` (`type: 'object'`) on the gate-wrapped registration. All eight RIGHT; each file names the block and the key the locator asks for.

7. **Check-runs on the head:** 43 check-runs, read settled at 2026-10-02T01:29Z after one bounded poll: 40 success, 3 skipped by design (`dependabot`, `Test (coverage)`, the coverage shard), 0 failed, 0 in progress. The eight test shards, `Test (dist pins)`, `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Spec Main Shape Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, the changeset gates and the doc gates are all green. These conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing was built, run or re-run locally. The finding in item 4 is a description clause no gate reads, which is why every gate is green beside it.

### ② Semver level

- `@object-ui/plugin-timeline` `minor`: ten inputs and an optional `objectName` widen the published authoring surface; the narrowing is the page validator moving to what the row already refuses (off-list `dateFormat` → `invalid-enum` error, non-array `data` → `type-mismatch` warning), and `objectui validate` refused both already by reference to the row. Same class and level as slice 1 (`yes (narrowing)`, `minor`, PASSed). RIGHT.
- `@object-ui/plugin-kanban` and `@object-ui/plugin-calendar` `patch`: one description clause each, behaviour unchanged. RIGHT.
- No `apps/console` changeset: test-only, the slice 4 precedent. RIGHT.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`: `clause2-line.mjs` reads value `yes`, arm `narrowing` (the first token inside the parenthetical after the value), and the line states both halves. RIGHT.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **`open_questions[0]`, the `descriptionField` describe contradiction.** The PR changes no renderer line and no spec text; the description keeps the describe's true sentence and states the measured order, so neither A (upstream corrects the describe) nor B (the renderer stops reading `mapping.description`) is pre-empted. Not half-decided. The seat's booking stands (file upstream after landing); nothing is ruled here.
2. **`TimelineConfigSchema.scale` `.default('week')` against the gantt branch's `month`** (dev: noted, not filed). The description claims no default, which is right. Escalated to the seat: file it on the same upstream card as item 1 rather than leave it noted, since the parsed state (`ObjectTimelinePropsParsed`) materializes `week` where the renderer draws `month`.
3. **Dev deviations.** `Clause-②` arm `yes (narrowing)`: right (②). The `sort` rewrite and the `objectName` description beyond the ten keys: inside the block's judgment, right. The shared list on `view:timeline`: right. H5 found only in the two registrations: right, the READMEs and docs pages do not carry it. The read-site comment corrected with the JSDoc: right. Census 7 → 8 red rows: the partition row is the same fact. Suites at `e068eedce` with the final union at `7364c4449`: the head's check-runs are the verdict (① 7).
4. **The dropped `required` reaches the `navigation` description** (① 4): the FAIL, one round. The PR body's own validator table (`items` only → none) is the measurement that opens the case.
